title: Playing cello then bass at lawn parties
summary: How he moved from cello to picking bass and what the lawn parties were like: dress, lighting and the yards.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Waiting for the band to come. Yeah. Did you say you played cello before you cut the bass? Mm-hmm. I played a dollar and a half in my cello. Did you pick that too, just like a bass?
Oh no. Or did you blow it? I used a little bow then. See, I started picking string bass after my brother got a bass. I played the lawn party.
I forget what year it was. Was that in New Orleans or in the country? No, it is. Uh-huh, no.
Did people dress up for those lawn parties or just come the way they were? Dress up.

You see, back in those days you had what you called gigum, gigum dresses, you know. But there's very good gigum. Good boy, I see. The girls looked very good. There was no, see when you get a girl, whatever color she was, you seen that. Because they didn't have all that makeup because girls back in the days, they put any makeup on their face, they call them bad. See, because all the sport women was made up there and the guys were sure. Yes. See, they didn't makeup back in those days. Better not to catch a girl making up, man. The father knocked a block off. They didn't believe in all that. If you didn't have, if you had a rosy cheeses until just there, there was no made rosy cheeses. Yes. See, because girls, like I see these kids going to school now, putting ruse on their lips. Better not go do that. See, the sport women did that. Yeah. Like red stockings. Flashy clothes. Sport women wear that, not the...
How were the men dressed at those lawn parties?

They dressed very good. They were silk shirts. Ties? Most of them didn't wear no ties. No ties. Just shirt, no coat. No. Sometime they were wearing, sometime they were no coat. Had a big diamond horseshoe pin, ring on like I got here. Uh-huh. Diamond horseshoe pin, and that's... Were those lawn parties in the daytime or in the... At night, in the night. I have lights with... You ever saw... What's those things they put candles in the... What the hell they call them? Paper things you mean? Yeah, they put the candles on each side. What the hell they call them?

Yeah, but they didn't call them that down there. What the hell they call them? Well, anyhow, they have those all around the yard. No liquid lights, you know. Have those candles, you know. And they have a big oil lamp. Then they have two, three big oil lamps. Be enough light. The most light is where they come in, where they pay and where... So they get a caliber money. Where the guys sell the beer, ice cream. Yes.
What kind of places would they hold lawn parties like that?
Any yard, clean it up. Big yard.
Oh, you mean it was out in the open air, huh? Yeah.
I see. They'd have some time, they'd have a little topo, you know, with a band. There's a red topo, you can put it with a band, you know. All the kind of dampness that night for the instruments.
